name: Isolated Proximal Femoral Focal Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for PFFD

criteria.description: Congenital shortening or absence of the proximal femur
Absence or hypoplasia of the femoral head on imaging
Normal development of the contralateral femur and lower limb

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital proximal femoral shortening or absence plus femoral head hypoplasia or absence confirmed by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by radiographic findings; genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving the femoral head and neck

imaging: Radiographs showing absent or hypoplastic proximal femur and femoral head
MRI or CT confirming femoral head absence and acetabular dysplasia
Ultrasound may be used in neonates for hip joint evaluation
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; etiology is largely sporadic
other: Clinical examination revealing limb length discrepancy and hip instability

distinguishingFeatures: Involvement of fibula with foot deformities
Short femur without absence or hypoplasia of femoral head

redFlags: Severe limb length discrepancy causing functional impairment
Hip joint instability leading to dislocation
references: Paley D. Proximal femoral focal deficiency: classification and management. Clin Orthop Relat Res. 1984;(182):40-50.
Orphanet: Proximal femoral focal deficiency. Orphanet Report Series. 2023.
Hunter JB, et al. Imaging of congenital femoral deficiencies. Radiographics. 2015;35(6):1747-1760.
